newsitem.title: MALDIVES: India, Pakistan leaders agree prisoner release.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan leaders agree prisoner release.

text.p: The leaders of India and Pakistan said they had agreed in their first talks for four years on Monday to release all prisoners from each others' countries.
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, said they also agreed during a 90-minute meeting to establish a telephone hotline.
"We agreed to a hotline between both of us," Gujral told reporters after the meeting an at island resort in the Maldives.

Sharif said the two leaders agreed to establish working groups to address various outstanding issues dividing the two South Asian nations, and that their countries' foreign secretaries would perhaps meet in Islamabad next month to pursue bilateral talks.
Gujral called his first face-to-face meeting with Sharif "very warm, very friendly", while the Pakistani leader said the talks were very constructive.
"I like the man very much," Sharif said of his Indian counterpart.
